_comment: Sigma correlation rules can't be compiled to a single query string (the Elasticsearch backend refuses: 'Backend does not support correlation rules'), so this is the Kibana Elasticsearch query rule config maintained by hand. This is the exact configuration that raised an alert against a Kerbrute spray in the lab on 25 Nov 2026.
name: Password Spray - Kerberos Pre-Auth Failures
_known_limitations: The Sigma rule groups by source IP and counts distinct usernames. This config does neither. In the lab's Winlogbeat 8.12 output, winlog.event_data.IpAddress and source.address are empty on 4771 events, and source.ip is an IP-type field the Elasticsearch query rule type can't group on. With a group-by on an empty field the rule never fires.
Counting all 4771 events across the domain works with one attacker in a lab. In production it can't name the source, and ordinary mistyped passwords can add up and trigger it.
Proper fix: an ingest pipeline that copies the client IP into a keyword field, then group by it and use aggType cardinality on winlog.event_data.TargetUserName.
The Sigma base rule also includes 4625. The deployed rule was only tested with 4771.
